notes: POWO and FNA accept A. incanum.
Both current POWO and FNA list its U.S. native range west of Texas (Arizona/Colorado/New Mexico), making the Hays-local pool record a likely re-ID or range-conflict target.

target_zone_range_leads.guardrail: Scout research only. Deep Review must verify exact target-zone counties and resolve any nativity/re-identification conflict.
leads: Master Plant Pool marks Hays Local, but this conflicts with current POWO/FNA distribution.
POWO lists Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and western/northern Mexico, not Texas.
FNA likewise excludes Texas; do not count it as native without contrary authoritative evidence.

morphology_candidate.look_here_first: Start with the small reflexed flower and style count: densely gray-tomentose subshrub, yellow or pink petals often with a dark red center, and only five style branches.
diagnostic_traits: petals 4–6 mm, yellow or pink, often dark red at center

confusers.separator: A. fruticosum has plain yellow flowers, 6–9 style branches, and is currently documented native in Texas; A. incanum often has a dark-centered smaller reflexed corolla and five styles.

photo_candidates.role: yellow flower with dark red center + buds
